newsitem.title: USA: Bush Boake hampered by exchange rates.
newsitem.headline: Bush Boake hampered by exchange rates.

text.p: Flavors and fragrances supplier Bush Boake Allen Inc said on Friday that unfavorable currency exchanges had a less-than-rosy effect on some of its operations last quarter, but that demand for the company's products appeared to be solid.
Bush Boake Allen said volume and margins had been adversely affected, for example, by a strong pound sterling, making "it much more difficult to export from the U.K. to the European Continent."
The company, which has locations in 41 countries, also named currency exchange rates as a factor contributing to a more competitive environment in the Asia Pacific Region.
"Market demand for the company's products currently appears to be solid in spite of some disadvantageous currency exchange situations," chief executive Julian Boyden said.

Bush Boake Allen, which supplies flavors and fragrance for use in foods, soaps and cosmetics, reported second quarter earnings of $0.44 per share on revenues of 125.7 million, compared with earnings of $0.52 per share on revenues of $113.5 million for the year-ago period.
Earnings results for 1996, however, included a net gain of $0.14 per share from the sale of land in Widnes, U.K.
